html:
Léon M'ba was the first president of Gabon, leading it from independence in 1960 until his death in 1967.

A Fang from Libreville, he worked as a clerk and a canton chief under French rule and was exiled for years to Ubangi-Shari. He became head of government in 1959 and president when Gabon left French Equatorial Africa as an independent state in August 1960.

He favoured close ties with France, and when officers overthrew him in the coup of February 1964, French paratroopers put him back in power within a day. He grew more authoritarian afterwards. Before he died he chose the young Albert-Bernard Bongo as his vice president and heir.
